questions.q: The number of floods in a decade is a…
questions.why: It takes countable values (0, 1, 2…), so probabilities can be assigned to exact values.

options: bell shaped and symmetric around its mean
flat, with every value equally likely
questions.why: Most observations sit near the mean, with fewer in the tails.

questions.q: We have data for every county in North Carolina. Why do geographers still use probability?
options: We don't. With the whole population, probability doesn't apply
The observed pattern is treated as one possible outcome of an underlying process
Because counties are always a random sample
questions.why: This is the idea of a natural sample: the map we see is one realization of a process that could have played out differently.
